name: Jetonomy

qa_actions.gate: ZERO FAIL lines. The total is a tripwire for accidentally-skipped phases, not the pass condition.
qa_actions.note: 286 is the total on a site where BuddyNext/WPMediaVerse is active. WPMediaVerse owns messaging site-wide, so Private_Messaging\Extension::is_dormant() is true, its REST routes are deliberately not registered, and Phase 3 skips the PM group by design (Basecamp 10150583760) - enabling the extension in jetonomy_pro_extensions does NOT change this and is not a fix. On a site WITHOUT WPMediaVerse the PM group runs and the total is HIGHER. Re-stamp this field, with verified_on_site, whenever a release adds or removes tests or the gate moves to a different site.

_wp_path_note: Deliberately null. This field is machine-specific and fails SILENTLY when stale: it previously pointed at /Users/vapvarun/Local Sites/buddynext/app/public, which does not exist on other machines, while base_url pointed at buddynext.local - a site carrying its OWN jetonomy copy at 1.9.2 on main. A smoke run would have certified 1.9.2 and stamped the report with the release version. Derive the WP root three levels up from the plugin directory instead, per the wp-plugin-smoke skill.

model_env.why: Without this constant the Pro licence check fails, all 17 extensions never boot, zero jetonomy-pro/v1 REST routes register, and EVERY E and S check is reported as 'skipped' while the run still reads as a pass. The 2026-09-02 smoke skipped all 20 Pro checks for exactly this reason, in a release that shipped a Pro fix. Verify with: wp eval 'printf("%d\n", count(\Jetonomy_Pro::instance()->get_extensions()));' - expect 17, not 0.

coverage_gate.why: The build gate previously checked only that `failures` held no 'from' entries plus a version match, so a run that skipped 47 of 84 checks - including every Pro check - still satisfied it. Absence of failures is not coverage.
